title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: This bill establishes requirements for creating and delivering detailed functional bills of materials for AI systems, helping stakeholders understand how AI components are built and sourced. It also includes supplementary measures to support transparency, accountability, and related regulatory objectives.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act aims to build a skilled workforce that can develop and oversee trustworthy AI systems. It focuses on training, education, and professional standards to ensure AI is developed and managed responsibly.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 sets out rules and standards to reduce the energy use and carbon footprint of AI systems, from data centers to training and deployment. It creates a regulatory body to monitor emissions, enforce compliance, and promote greener AI technologies through incentives and reporting requirements.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to prevent companies from using artificial intelligence to unjustifiably raise prices or manipulate wage levels. It establishes regulations and penalties to protect consumers and workers from unfair pricing and wage practices.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 aims to regulate the environmental effects of AI systems, focusing on reducing their energy consumption and carbon footprint. It establishes guidelines and reporting requirements for developers and users to ensure AI technologies are designed, deployed, and maintained in an environmentally responsible manner.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to prevent AI companies from exploiting consumers through inflated prices and from manipulating labor markets to suppress wages. It establishes regulations and penalties to ensure fair pricing and equitable compensation for workers in the AI sector.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 establishes regulations for the use of artificial intelligence in the agriculture sector, focusing on ensuring transparency, safety, and accountability for AI‑driven farming technologies. The act outlines standards for data privacy, algorithmic fairness, and mandates oversight to protect farmers and consumers from potential misuse of AI in food production.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: This act aims to accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence across the financial services sector by providing a clear regulatory framework. It encourages innovation while ensuring consumer protection, data privacy, and market stability through oversight and compliance requirements.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The “Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act” is designed to encourage the development and adoption of AI technologies within the financial sector by providing clear guidelines and regulatory support. It aims to promote innovation while ensuring consumer protection, data privacy, and market stability through updated legal frameworks and compliance requirements.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act aims to strengthen the nation's AI workforce by providing training, education, and incentives for individuals and companies to develop advanced AI skills. It outlines policies and funding mechanisms that support research, talent development, and innovation in artificial intelligence.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act prohibits the establishment of artificial‑intelligence data centers on any federal land. It is intended to protect federal property, safeguard environmental and privacy concerns, and reduce potential security risks associated with large‑scale data center operations.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is designed to integrate artificial intelligence education into American schools from kindergarten through 12th grade. It aims to equip students with the skills and knowledge needed to safely navigate and responsibly use AI technologies in their future academic and professional lives.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students from kindergarten through 12th grade with foundational knowledge about artificial intelligence. It establishes standards, curricula, and teacher training programs so schools can responsibly and safely teach AI concepts.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires companies that develop or deploy artificial‑intelligence systems in China to submit detailed reports on their AI‑related energy consumption, efficiency, and carbon impact. The act aims to monitor and regulate AI’s contribution to national energy usage, ensuring that AI development aligns with China’s broader environmental and technology policy goals.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to set clear rules for how artificial intelligence systems are designed, tested, and used in the United States. It focuses on protecting public safety, privacy, and accountability while encouraging responsible innovation in AI technology.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act seeks to equip teachers and students with knowledge about AI tools, their benefits, and potential risks. It establishes guidelines, training programs, and accountability measures to ensure responsible use of AI in educational settings.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 sets new safety and design standards for AI-enabled toys sold to children, requiring manufacturers to meet strict testing and certification before the toys can enter the market. The act also establishes clear rules on data privacy, transparency of AI behavior, and liability for any harm caused by these toys.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives believes that anyone who could be affected by the construction or operation of an artificial‑intelligence data center—whether an individual or a community—has a right to clear and open information about those projects. They argue that people should also have a say in how these data centers are designed and run in their own neighborhoods.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 establishes standards for using AI technologies in veteran services, aiming to protect veterans' privacy, safety, and well‑being. It mandates that government agencies adopt transparent, ethical, and accountable AI practices, and creates oversight mechanisms to ensure AI tools benefit veterans without unintended harm.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The AI Act of 2026 aims to prevent the use of artificial intelligence for creating or spreading false or misleading content that could exploit people or communities. It establishes rules and safeguards to detect, limit, and penalize such fabricated exploitation, promoting transparency and accountability in AI systems.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a federal framework for studying how AI tools are used in the judicial system, requiring courts to evaluate and document their impact on fairness, accuracy, and transparency. It also creates an independent oversight body to monitor compliance, publish annual reports, and recommend policy adjustments to safeguard the integrity of the justice system.

title: A bill to require a report on the use of artificial intelligence with respect to access to unminimized information collected pursuant to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The bill requires lawmakers to produce a report on how artificial intelligence is used when accessing unminimized intelligence data collected under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report also covers other aspects of AI usage and broader implications.

title: Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Decoupling America’s Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 is designed to cut U.S. dependence on Chinese AI technology by restricting the import, use, and development of Chinese AI hardware, software, and data. It seeks to protect national security, boost domestic AI innovation, and establish clear rules for U.S. companies engaging with Chinese AI firms.

title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 aims to stop AI systems from secretly coordinating to fix prices or manipulate markets, protecting competition and consumers. It establishes reporting requirements, enforcement powers, and penalties to ensure companies disclose and monitor algorithmic behaviors that could lead to collusive outcomes.
